title: How to get better iPhone battery life without closing any apps
content_md: The app switcher is not the cause of your battery problem. In fact, Apple’s own documentation on app behavior says something different The gap between what the switcher suggests and what iOS actually does is where most iPhone battery life advice goes wrong. This guide covers the settings that genuinely reduce power use , all of them built into your iPhone. These include screen settings, the power-saving mode, and background activity controls that stop apps working when you are not using them. Key takeaways The app switcher is not the cause of your battery problem. The display is the largest single consumer of power on any iPhone. Low Power Mode does the heavy lifting by limiting background activity. Settings -> Battery ranks apps by how much charge they consumed over the last day. Background App Refresh and location access are the two controls worth adjusting. Does closing apps improve iPhone battery life? No, not in the way most people assume. When you switch away from an app, iOS suspends it. Suspended means paused until needed .
